english.title: Fail to keep a record of risk assessment
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) having carried out an assessment under section

(A)_[108(1)(a)]_
(B)_[108(3)(a)]_

of the Environmental Protection Act 1990, failed to keep, for the prescribed period, such record of the assessment as was prescribed
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 108(5) and 118(1)(e) and (6) of the Environmental Protection Act 1990.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
carry out s.108(1)(a) / (3)(a) assessment
fail to keep record of assessment for prescribed period

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
Whilst the wording of this offence is in force, it should be noted that neither section 108(1)(a) or 108(3)(a) are fully in force.
Therefore it is suggested that there should be caution in checking the current situation before prosecuting.

other.penalty:
Summary: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: Two years imprisonment and / or a fine.

Note:
Whilst the wording of this offence is in force, it should be noted that neither section 108(1)(a) or 108(3)(a) is yet in force.
Therefore it is suggested that there should not be any prosecutions under this section until they are in force.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
